five_whys_trace.q: Why build a document store now, rather than waiting for the search PRD that actually needs indexed text?
five_whys_trace.a: rag_indexer scores 61.8% against an 81.4% overall baseline (wiki 2026-09-23-mcphost-market-test-plan) and 'RAG index refresh' recurs in three independent discovery panels -- but search has nothing to index without a document identity, version, and change watermark existing first; this PRD is the prerequisite, not the fix itself (Success metrics: 'this PRD moves it only in combination' with the recipe PRD).

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a document need a version and a per-tenant seq watermark, not just an overwrite-in-place KV value the way host.state already works?
five_whys_trace.a: The indexer user story needs to answer 'what changed since I last looked' without scanning every document on every tick -- a per-tenant monotonic seq bumped only on a real change (requirement 1) is a changefeed a search index can page through with list {since}, the same shape meter_events/ban_hits already use for their own append-only event logs, just applied to a mutable-with-history resource instead.

five_whys_trace.q: Why store extracted text separately from raw content, computed once at put time, rather than extracting on every get?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 3's own wording -- 'the extracted text is what search will index and what get {text: true} returns' -- means the search PRD will read this same stored text on a hot indexing path; computing it once at write time (the same 'the write is where the expensive/authoritative work happens' shape host.export's tar-gz build already follows) keeps every later read O(1) instead of repeating JSON-flatten/CSV-parse work per read.

five_whys_trace.q: Why reject a sniffed binary format (e.g. image/png) even when the caller never declared a mime at all, rather than defaulting silently to text/plain?
five_whys_trace.a: AC8's own scenario is exactly this: no explicit mime, and the document is refused naming the allowed mimes. A document store whose 'text' extraction defaulted to lossy-decoding arbitrary binary bytes as UTF-8 would silently corrupt exactly the documents most likely to be a mistake (a caller who meant to attach an image), and would poison the search index the next PRD builds on top of this one.

five_whys_trace.q: Why keep blobs in a table (document_blobs) instead of the filesystem, when 2 MiB documents could get large in aggregate?
five_whys_trace.a: Technical considerations: 'blobs are stored in SQLite (no filesystem paths) so backup and export cover them' -- the same reasoning tables.rs's own per-tenant SQLite files and tenant_state_rows's JSON blobs already follow in this crate; a filesystem path would need its own backup/restore story and its own tenant-delete-cascade path instead of getting both for free from the existing mcphost.db ON DELETE CASCADE.
